title: Punishing an opening mistake: find it, or develop calmly
outcomes: Finds the punishment when the opponent's move leaves a concrete target
Develops calmly when no punishment exists
Does not mistake a greedy capture for a punishment
Asks what the last move left undefended or undeveloped before choosing

steps.text: In **Why a quick attack on f7 usually fails** a punishment needed a concrete reason. Now the mistake may be there or not. After the opponent's move ask: what did it leave undeveloped or loose? Do I have a move that uses it now? Does the greedy capture cost me more than it wins? If not, develop. Calm is a good answer. First, an early queen.

**Rule of thumb for the opening:** a punishment needs development on your side and a target on theirs. It fails when the target is defended, when the capture opens your own king, or when the move was simply fine. 'Punish at once' is a misconception: some moves cost the other side nothing you can reach. Next: three positions, one kind of question. Predict first.

steps.title: Punish, refuse or ignore?
steps.prompt: Black has made an odd move in each position. In which does a punishment exist? Predict, then check.
Write the two things you check after any odd-looking opening move. Then write a move of yours from a recent game that an opponent could have punished, and what would have been needed.
